'''Gihan Kamel''' is an Egyptian physicist known for her work as an Infrared Beamline Scientist in the [[Synchrotron-Light for Experimental Science and Applications in the Middle East|Synchrotron-light project for Experimental Science and Applications in the Middle East (SESAME).]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Dr. Gihan Kamel|url=http://worldscienceforum.org/participants/kamel-gihan-30971|access-date=2020-08-21|website=World Science Forum}}{{Dead link|date=June 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=We do not fight when we deal with science – Dr Gihan Kamel|url=https://horizon-magazine.eu/article/we-do-not-fight-when-we-deal-science-dr-gihan-kamel.html|access-date=2020-08-21|website=Horizon: the EU Research & Innovation magazine|language=en|archive-date=2021-01-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210125041037/https://horizon-magazine.eu/article/we-do-not-fight-when-we-deal-science-dr-gihan-kamel.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> She lives in [[Jordan]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Gihan Kamel {{!}} Women in Optics {{!}} SPIE|url=https://spie.org/about-spie/advocacy/women-in-optics/women-in-optics-planner/2017-wio-planner/gihan-kamel|access-date=2020-08-21|website=spie.org}}</ref>

== Education and early life ==
Gihan's mother is a doctor and her father is a teacher. The "idea that science and engineering were meant only for men became [her] strongest motivation"<ref name=":1" /> to pursue a career in science.

She studied [[physics]] at [[Helwan University]] in [[Cairo]], obtaining a [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] and an [[Master of Science|MSc]] in [[solid-state physics]]<ref name=":1" /> before moving to [[Italy]], where she obtained a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D]] in [[biophysics]] in 2011 at the [[Sapienza University of Rome]].<ref name=":0" />

== Career and research ==
She is a lecturer in Biophysics at Helwan University,<ref name=":0" /> and since the mid-2000s she has been interested in the [[Synchrotron-Light for Experimental Science and Applications in the Middle East|SESAME]] project, which brings together nine countries (Bahrain, Cyprus, Egypt, Jordan, Pakistan, Turkey, Palestine, Iran and Israel), and is currently the only woman scientist on the project.<ref name=":0" />

In 2015, she earned recognition for her presentation at a TED conference on the theme of "Breaking the Rules".<ref>{{Cite web|title=TEDxCERN {{!}} TED|url=https://www.ted.com/tedx/events/15188|access-date=2020-08-21|website=www.ted.com}}</ref>

In 2023, she was one of the six women chosen by ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' journal to comment on their plans for [[International Women's Day]]. The others were [[Sandra Díaz (ecologist)|Sandra Diaz]], [[Martina Anto-Ocrah]], [[Jess Wade]], [[Aster Gebrekirstos]] and [[Tanya Monro]].<ref>{{Cite journal |date=2023-03-08 |title=Celebrate women in science — today, and every day |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-023-00670-5 |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=615 |issue=7951 |pages=187–187 |doi=10.1038/d41586-023-00670-5|doi-access=free }}</ref>

In 2025, Gihan received the [[John Wheatley Award]] with [[Simon Connell]] and [[Sekazi Mtingwa]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gihan Kamel awarded the John Wheatley Award 2025 |url=https://www.sesame.org.jo/news/gihan-kamel-awarded-john-wheatley-award-2025 |access-date=2024-12-28 |website=www.sesame.org.jo |language=en}}</ref>
